Various explanations of the other elements of the word have been suggested, but none of them are supported by convincing evidence. One by the American linguist Richard Lederer (born 1938) in his book Crazy English (1989) is super- + cali- (a variant of calli- (prefix meaning ‘beautiful’)) + fragilistic- (from fragile (“delicate”)) + expiali- (from expiate (“to atone or make reparation for”)) + docious (“amenable to order, docile”), suggesting that the word means “atoning for extreme and delicate beauty [while being] highly educable”.
